articles.title: The Foxglove Heights Neighbors Opens Tool Library on Harbor Terrace
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 5 people and say tool library is the main draw.
body: The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The effort began in May when a handful of neighbors met at the Mill Hill town hall to talk about tool library.
Several residents on Harbor Terrace said they had been waiting since 1993 for something like this. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Tuesday mornings.

Leona Dunmore, who has lived on Harbor Terrace for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The Mill Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.

body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Eastgate said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Letter: The Free Tax Clinic on Mulberry Lane Needs Attention
body: To the editor: I have lived on Mulberry Lane for 8 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made. Please keep the free tax clinic in the budget. Many of us on Mulberry Lane use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting.

To the editor: I have lived on Mulberry Lane for 8 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made. Please keep the free tax clinic in the budget. Many of us on Mulberry Lane use it every week.
Carol McIver, Tannery Flats
